# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration ("dual-run" architecture), allowing per-user cutover and safe rollback at any stage. Migration proceeds in five named phases, each gated by an explicit entry criterion, with continuous monitoring against halt thresholds.

---

## Phase 1: "Canary" — 0.5% of users (~200 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging (100% of test suite green, including invoice generation, payment capture, refunds, and proration edge cases), and a rollback script capable of reverting a user to the old system within 15 minutes has been validated in a dry run.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-ARPU test customers only — no enterprise or high-value accounts.

**Duration:** Minimum 7 days of stable operation before proceeding.

---

## Phase 2: "Early Adopters" — 5% of users (~2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero critical (Sev-1) incidents, billing discrepancy rate under threshold (see Metrics below), and support ticket volume from Phase 1 cohort no greater than 1.5x the baseline rate for the old system.

**Population:** Randomly sampled across low-to-mid tier plans, excluding annual-contract enterprise customers.

**Duration:** Minimum 10 days.

---

## Phase 3: "Broad Rollout" — 35% of users (~14,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 discrepancy and incident metrics remain within threshold for the full duration, reconciliation reports between old and new systems match within tolerance for 10 consecutive days, and finance/accounting has signed off on general-ledger parity for Phase 2 cohort.

**Population:** General customer base across all plan tiers, still excluding largest enterprise accounts and customers with custom contractual billing terms.

**Duration:** Minimum 14 days, migrated in weekly sub-batches (e.g., ~3,500/week) to preserve observability.

---

## Phase 4: "Remaining Majority + Enterprise" — 49.5% of users (~19,800 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 cumulative discrepancy rate stays within threshold, no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents open for more than 48 hours, and enterprise accounts have had a dedicated dry-run reconciliation (shadow billing run compared against legacy invoices for at least one full billing cycle) with zero material variance.

**Population:** Remaining standard customers plus enterprise/custom-contract accounts, migrated last due to complexity and revenue sensitivity. Enterprise accounts get individual account-manager notification and a scheduled maintenance window.

**Duration:** Minimum 21 days, with enterprise accounts migrated in the final week of this phase to allow maximum bake time for the bulk of Phase 4 before touching highest-value contracts.

---

## Phase 5: "Verification & Stabilization" — 0% new migrations (validation-only phase covering 100% of migrated users)

**Entry criterion:** All 40,000 users have been migrated (Phase 4 complete) and a full billing cycle (at least one monthly invoice run) has completed successfully on the new system for the final batch.

**Purpose:** Run both systems in parallel in read-only/shadow mode for the old system, complete full financial reconciliation across all cohorts, obtain finance and compliance sign-off, and only then schedule decommissioning of the old billing system as a separate, subsequent change — never bundled with the final migration batch itself.

---

## Metrics with Halt Thresholds

- **Billing discrepancy rate:** If more than **0.1%** of migrated users' invoices in any 24-hour window show a monetary discrepancy greater than $1.00 versus the shadow calculation on the old system, halt all further migrations in the current phase and freeze the phase population.
- **Payment failure rate delta:** If the new system's payment failure/decline rate exceeds the old system's baseline by more than **20% relative** over a rolling 48-hour window, halt.
- **Support ticket surge:** If billing-related support tickets from the migrated cohort exceed **2x** the pre-migration baseline rate for that cohort over any 72-hour window, halt and investigate before resuming.
- **Reconciliation lag:** If the automated ledger reconciliation job fails to complete or shows unmatched transaction volume greater than **0.05%** of total transaction count for two consecutive runs, halt.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-charging of customers during dual-run overlap window | Implement idempotency keys and a single source-of-truth billing-state flag per user, plus automated daily reconciliation between both systems | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Data mapping errors for complex pricing plans (proration, discounts, usage-based tiers) causing incorrect invoice amounts | Run shadow billing in parallel for at least one full cycle per cohort before cutover and require finance sign-off on variance reports | Finance Systems Analyst
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated too early and suffer invoicing errors that damage the relationship | Migrate enterprise accounts last, in Phase 4, with individual dry-run reconciliation and account-manager involvement | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Rollback mechanism fails under real load, leaving affected users stuck on a broken new-system state | Validate rollback procedure in staging under load test before Phase 1, and re-validate after each phase before proceeding | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Old billing system is decommissioned prematurely alongside final migration batch, removing the safety net before reconciliation is complete | Enforce a mandatory Phase 5 verification period and require explicit finance/compliance sign-off as a separate approval gate before any decommissioning ticket can be filed | Program Manager

PHASES: 5
